title: Orbital propellant depots as economic infrastructure
bottleneck: The physics of depots is understood, but the business case is not: a depot operator must invest billions in cryogenic infrastructure before any customer exists, while launch providers have little incentive to standardize refueling interfaces that commoditize their vehicles. Insurance, liability for a depot full of cryogenics, and the chicken-and-egg problem of demand have kept depots as presentation architecture for 20 years, even as Starship makes refueling technically mandatory for Artemis.
why_it_blocks: Without depots, every deep-space mission must launch fully fueled in one shot, capping payload mass; the depot is the difference between flags-and-footprints missions and real logistics.
current_state: Starship's 2024 intra-vehicle transfer demo and a planned inter-vehicle demo are the first real steps; ULA's distributed-launch studies keep the concept alive. No operational depot exists.

sources.title: Propellant depots: an idea whose time has (almost) come (The Space Review)
